questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionMarkup:
Astronomer: Most stars are born in groups of thousands, each star in a group forming from the same parent cloud of gas. Each cloud has a unique homogeneous chemical composition. Therefore whenever two stars have the same chemical composition as each other, they must have originated from the same cloud of gas.
Which of the following, if true, would most strengthen the astronomer’s argument?
questions.questionText: Astronomer: Most stars are born in groups of thousands, each star in a group forming from the same parent cloud of gas. Each cloud has a unique homogeneous chemical composition. Therefore whenever two stars have the same chemical composition as each other, they must have originated from the same cloud of gas. Which of the following, if true, would most strengthen the astronomer’s argument?

options.html: In some groups of stars, not every star originated from the same parent cloud of gas.
options.text: In some groups of stars, not every star originated from the same parent cloud of gas.

options.html: Clouds of gas of similar or identical chemical composition may be remote from each other.
options.text: Clouds of gas of similar or identical chemical composition may be remote from each other.

options.html: Whenever a star forms, it inherits the chemical composition of its parent cloud of gas.
options.text: Whenever a star forms, it inherits the chemical composition of its parent cloud of gas.

options.html: Many stars in vastly different parts of the universe are quite similar in their chemical compositions.
options.text: Many stars in vastly different parts of the universe are quite similar in their chemical compositions.

questions.explanationHtml:
(c)
It is given that each cloud has a unique homogeneous chemical composition and the stars originated from the same cloud of gas have the same chemical composition. Thus, it can be concluded that whenever a star forms, it inherits the chemical composition of its parent cloud of gas. Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.questionMarkup:
People tend to estimate the likelihood of an event’s occurrence according to its salience; that is, according to how strongly and how often it comes to their attention. By placement and headlines, newspapers emphasize stories about local crime over stories about crime elsewhere and about many other major events.
It can be concluded on the basis of the statements above that, if they are true, which of the following is most probably also true?
questions.questionText: People tend to estimate the likelihood of an event’s occurrence according to its salience; that is, according to how strongly and how often it comes to their attention. By placement and headlines, newspapers emphasize stories about local crime over stories about crime elsewhere and about many other major events. It can be concluded on the basis of the statements above that, if they are true, which of the following is most probably also true?

options.html: The language used in newspaper headlines about local crime is inflammatory and fails to respect the rights of suspects.
options.text: The language used in newspaper headlines about local crime is inflammatory and fails to respect the rights of suspects.

options.html: The press is the news medium that focuses people attention most strongly on local crimes.
options.text: The press is the news medium that focuses people attention most strongly on local crimes.

options.html: Readers of local news in newspapers tend to overestimate the amount of crime in their own localities relative to the amount of crime in other places.
options.text: Readers of local news in newspapers tend to overestimate the amount of crime in their own localities relative to the amount of crime in other places.

options.html: None of the events concerning other people that are reported in newspapers is so salient in people’s minds as their own personal experiences.
options.text: None of the events concerning other people that are reported in newspapers is so salient in people’s minds as their own personal experiences.

questions.explanationHtml:
(c)
We know that newspapers’ coverage of local crimes is stronger than that of non-local crimes.
Nothing is said about frequency of coverage so, we can not assume anything about it. However, all else being equal, we can assume that people tend to think the local crimes outnumber non-local crimes.
